messages.text: What size should i get for my homeschool

For homeschool use, you want a globe that's big enough to read easily and ideally has raised relief so kids can feel mountain ranges while they learn. Since you're already looking at the Quincy line, I'd point you toward a 12-inch globe rather than the 9-inch — the larger map surface makes country names and borders much easier for kids to read during lessons, and it still fits nicely on a desk or table.

Would this be for one child's desk, or something the whole family would gather around to study?

For a family that'll gather around it together, I'd point you to the 12" Interactive Talking World Globe with Wireless Intelli-Pen. It has raised relief terrain kids can feel, and the talking pen lets them tap countries for facts — great for mixed ages learning together, and the 12" size is easy for everyone to see at once. If you'd rather have something larger that stands in a shared room as a bigger focal point for lessons, a 16-inch floor globe would give you more map to explore at a glance, though it won't have the interactive pen feature.

Do your kids span a wide range of ages, or close together?
i want to avoid anything illuminated or interactive

Got it — for a family homeschool setup without lights or tech, the Trafalgar 16-inch Blue Ocean Floor Globe is a strong fit: it's raised relief so kids can feel mountain ranges, the blue ocean map is the classic crisp, easy-to-read style for studying borders and place names, and at 16 inches it's big enough for several kids to gather around at once. If you'd rather keep it on a tabletop instead of the floor, a 12-inch blue ocean desk globe with raised relief would give the same reading clarity in a smaller footprint.

Is this going in a dedicated school space, or a common room everyone shares?

The Trafalgar 16-inch Blue Ocean Floor Globe is a great pick for a common room — it stands on its own as a piece of furniture everyone can walk up to and spin, and at 16 inches the whole family can read it together without crowding a desk. You'll find it under that exact name in search, ready to add to your cart.

What's prompting the homeschool switch, if you don't mind my asking — just curious how you landed here?
